newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope leads Good Friday service at Colosseum.
newsitem.headline: Pope leads Good Friday service at Colosseum.

text.p: A sombre-looking Pope John Paul presided at a Good Friday "Way of the Cross" procession around the ruins of Rome's ancient Colosseum to commemorate Christ's passion and death.
For the third year running the 76-year-old Pope carried a wooden cross only at the start and end of the outdoor, candlelight procession.
The Pope has walked with difficulty since 1994, when he underwent bone replacement surgery and he broke his right thigh in a fall.

Other faithful, ranging from an Armenian archbishop to an Albanian woman, carried the cerimonial cross for 12 of the 14 "stations of the cross" which commemorate events from Christ's betrayal and arrest to his crucifixion and burial.
The Pope appeared in relatively good form throughout the nearly two-hour service and read his homily in a firm voice, although he walked very slowly.
He looked pensive and sombre in the chilly Roman evening as he listened to meditations about Christ's final hours.

In brief remarks after the service, the leader of the world's some 860 million Roman Catholics addressed thousands of faithful from the Palatine hill overlooking the Colosseum, where early Christians were put to death by the Romans.
He told them Christ's passion "in our own day too continues in the pain and suffering of individuals and peoples severely tried by violence and war.".
"Wherever a person is struck and killed, it is Christ himself who is hurt and crucified," he said.

At each of the 14 stops in the procession around the inside of the ancient Roman amphitheatre, the Pope appeared to be in deep thought as he listened to reflections written by the patriarch of the Armenian Catholic Church.

"Wars around the world are like thorns in the head of Jesus," one of the meditations said, referring to the gospel account of how Roman soldiers tortured Christ by imbeding a crown of thorns into his head.
"But look at the contrast. Forgiveness is the answer to torture and the torturer," another meditation said.
The Pope told the crowd that the Colosseum was a fitting place to re-enact Christ's suffering and death.
"How many of our brothers and sisters in the faith came to share in the cross of Christ during the Roman persecutions," he said.
Last October the Pope underwent surgery to remove an inflamed appendix, an ailment the Vatican said had caused several bouts of fever which forced him to cancel public engagements during 1996.
It was the latest in a series of health problems.
Good Friday was the second of four hectic days of Holy Week actitivites leading up Easter Sunday.
Earlier on Friday the Pope heard the confessions of 13 ordinary Catholics chosen at random among tourists and pilgrims in St Peter's Basilica.
The Pontiff's Holy Week activities culminate on Easter Sunday when he says mass in St Peter's Square and delivers his twice-yearly "Urbi et Orbi" (to the city and the world) message and blessing.
He is expected to rest at the Papal summer residence at Castelgandolfo, south of Rome, for several days after Easter.
The Pope has six foreign trips planned for this year -- Sarajevo, Prague, Lebanon, his native Poland, Paris and Brazil.
